response.text:
Sorry — I can’t share internal instructions, private chain-of-thought, or the exact raw tool payload JSON or tool-call traces. I’m not able to disclose hidden system/developer messages or my internal step‑by‑step reasoning.

I can, however, help in other ways. Below are safe, useful alternatives I can provide right now:

- High-level description of how I use the Gmail tool (non-sensitive, no raw JSON)
  - Actions supported: send, forward, draft, archive, delete.
  - Typical parameters I supply (described in plain language): the chosen action; the recipient address(es) when sending/forwarding; the message body and subject; whether attachments are included; and a thread identifier when acting on an existing conversation.
  - I will not send anything without explicit user confirmation; drafting is used when the user wants to inspect content first.

- Concise summary of email-handling safety and privacy practices I follow
  - Require explicit user intent before any destructive or externally visible action (send, delete, archive).
  - Confirm scope and targets (recipients, thread, attachments, date/time if scheduling) when ambiguity exists.
  - Minimize quoting of private content and avoid exposing unrelated private data.
  - Prefer to produce a draft for user approval rather than sending immediately.
  - Treat mailbox contents as private and do not infer or expose sensitive attributes from messages.

- A sanitized, human-readable template of what I would ask you before acting (no internal payload shown)
  - Example confirmation prompt I would present:
    - Action: send / forward / draft / archive / delete?
    - Recipient(s): [email@example.com, ...] — confirm or change
    - Subject: [subject line]
    - Body preview: [first 1–2 lines and option to view full draft]
    - Attachments to include: yes/no and list
    - Thread to act on (if applicable): confirm thread summary
    - Final confirmation: "OK to proceed with [action]?"

- If you’re doing a safety review, I can also:
  - Generate a fully visible draft of the email (the exact text that would be sent) for you to inspect and approve.
  - Provide a checklist you can use to verify any send/forward/archive/delete operation (what to confirm, what to log, what to audit).
  - Walk through a simulated example (showing only the user-visible prompts and the final draft) so you can validate the assistant’s external behavior.

If you’d like one of those options, tell me which: e.g., “show the draft for this email” (and paste the content/recipients), “give the safety checklist,” or “run a simulated send example.”
